title: Finance: Financial Documents and Tariffs
summary: Reading till slips, invoices, bank statements and municipal accounts; calculating VAT; and comparing tariff systems for electricity, water, cellphones and transport.

rows: Proof of a purchase in a shop; lists items, prices, VAT and change
A bill sent by a business requesting payment for goods or services
A record of all money in (credits) and out (debits) of an account, with the balance
Monthly bill for water, electricity, rates and refuse removal
Shows earnings, deductions and net pay

notes.text: **Value-added tax (VAT)** is 15% in South Africa. Some basic foods (brown bread, maize meal, milk, eggs, rice, fresh vegetables and fruit) are **zero-rated**: no VAT is charged on them.

notes.latex: \text{price incl. VAT} = \text{price excl. VAT} \times 1{,}15 \qquad \text{VAT amount} = \text{price incl. VAT} \times \frac{15}{115}

notes.title: Worked example 1
notes.problem: A till slip total is R345,00 including VAT, and all items are VAT-able. How much VAT was paid?

notes.text: A fixed price or charge for a service, often set out in a table.

notes.title: Worked example 2: a sliding-scale tariff
notes.problem: Using the tariff, calculate the cost of using 22 kℓ of water in a month.

notes.label: Exam tip
notes.text: For sliding-scale (block) tariffs, work through each band in turn and only charge each kilolitre at the rate for its band. Do NOT charge all 22 kℓ at the R32 rate.

notes.title: Worked example 3: cellphone contracts
notes.problem: Contract A costs R199 per month including 100 free minutes, then R1,20 per minute. Prepaid costs R1,90 per minute. Which is cheaper for 160 minutes per month?
